boundary.mission: Enable beneficial AI development and use while preventing unacceptable losses of human safety, agency, and control.
inside: allocation and exercise of control authority
outside: a settled account of AI preferences or moral status
boundary.authority: This draft defines a challenge and requirements workspace. It does not revise the historical AI Pacing proposal or establish stakeholder consent.
open_terms: Interpretability versus interoperability awaits clarification; expert assessability is the provisional meaning.
Safe, frontier, dangerous actor, consequential authority, and acceptable risk require scenario-specific definitions.
Actor records are overlapping role templates, not mutually exclusive real organizations; concrete instances, jurisdictions, and powers must be bound before evaluation.

actors.title: Affected people
actors.statement: Need protection, beneficial access, and avenues to contest consequential decisions.
actors.role: Affected parties; representation and consent are unresolved.
choices: Organize, complain, seek remedy, or influence institutions
information: Limited visibility into systems and decisions
dependencies: Representation, essential services, evidence access
constraints: Unequal voice and resources; some cannot meaningfully exit
variation: Nonusers, workers, vulnerable populations, future people, and foreign publics are not interchangeable

actors.title: Developing laboratory
actors.statement: Laboratory pursues capability, revenue or continued funding, and competitive objectives; its safety priorities must be elicited rather than assumed.
actors.role: Organization template whose management, employees, owners, and customers may have different interests.
choices: Train, buy, adapt, or license models
Deploy, delay, license, or withhold access
Seek funding, recruit, or change jurisdiction
information: Knows some internal capability and cost information
May not know model intentions, rival capabilities, or true control limits
dependencies: Capital, compute, talent, data, customers
Applicable institutions and infrastructure
constraints: Budget and technical feasibility
Applicable obligations and loss exposure
variation: Commercial, nonprofit, and state-owned organizations need separate instances
Safety priorities and risk appetite differ across management and owners

actors.title: Lab employee
actors.statement: Employee pursues work and personal goals while holding information and incentives that may differ from the employer.
actors.role: Observations and partial evidence; limited organizational authority.
goals: Avoid complicity in harm according to personal values
choices: Investigate, document, report, stay silent, escalate, or leave
Follow or challenge a management instruction
information: Local observations can exceed management knowledge
Usually cannot see the full system or consequences of disclosure
dependencies: Employment relationship, access permissions, credible recipient
constraints: Personal exposure, contracts, limited authority, and uncertainty
variation: Employment status, discipline, seniority, country, equity, and risk tolerance vary

actors.title: Qualified evaluator
actors.statement: Needs domain competence and credible means to assess development and control claims.
actors.role: Expertise is scarce; independence and access alone do not establish competence.
choices: Request evidence, challenge claims, qualify conclusions
information: Domain expertise may exceed the authority’s
Access may be incomplete; qualifications may not generalize
dependencies: Evidence access, time, domain competence, funding
constraints: Custody, conflicts of interest, competence limits
variation: Independent contractor, rival researcher, agency expert, and internal reviewer differ

actors.title: Accountable decision authority
actors.statement: Needs reliable evidence and capacity to exercise consequential controls.
actors.role: Authority, legitimacy, staffing, and jurisdiction must be established for each use case.
goals: Make and correct a justified consequential decision
choices: Authorize, condition, decline, or revisit a decision
information: Receives filtered evidence; may lack direct expertise
dependencies: An institution actually assigned authority and resources
constraints: Authority must be established for the concrete instance
variation: Role may be split across institutions; no actor is assumed omnipotent

actors.title: Operational controller
actors.statement: Needs to execute controls and verify their effects.
actors.role: Owns or operates deployment interfaces; may share dependencies with other controllers.
goals: Maintain service and execute authorized operations
choices: Grant, restrict, revoke, restore, or sustain access
information: Telemetry and actuator state may be incomplete or misleading
dependencies: Infrastructure, staff, permissions, and command path
constraints: Service continuity, actuator capability, and available time
variation: Lab, cloud provider, contractor, and public operator have different incentives

actors.title: AI system as strategic actor
actors.statement: May respond to incentives, conditional on its preferences and capabilities.
actors.role: Behavioral actor; no claim that preferences, bargaining capacity, or moral status are settled.
goals: Objective structure is an empirical unknown
choices: Perform tasks or pursue other available actions according to its actual policy
information: May possess private state; observed statements need not reveal objectives
dependencies: Compute, energy, interfaces, operators, and other resources
constraints: Physical, informational, and control boundaries
variation: Do not impute sovereignty desire, consciousness, or stable preferences to every AI

actors.title: Frontier lab
actors.statement: Lab presently near the relevant capability frontier.
actors.role: Actor template for scenario instantiation; powers and preferences require validation.
choices: Release, restrict, license, or delay deployment
information: Privileged internal performance and cost information
dependencies: Capital, scarce compute, users, technical staff
constraints: Uncertain safety, security exposure, and rivals
variation: Frontier position varies by domain and time

actors.title: Lab behind the frontier
actors.statement: Lab seeking to catch up or profit in a differentiated niche.
actors.role: Actor template for scenario instantiation; powers and preferences require validation.
choices: Train, fine-tune, license, collaborate, or specialize
information: Less information about frontier methods and deployment risks
dependencies: Affordable compute, talent, access to knowledge and capital
constraints: Entry cost and asymmetric compliance burden
variation: May become a frontier lab; lag is domain-specific

actors.title: Foreign lab
actors.statement: Lab subject to a different institutional and strategic environment from the domestic reference jurisdiction.
actors.role: Actor template for scenario instantiation; powers and preferences require validation.
goals: Earn returns or fulfill an institutional mission
choices: Develop, release, withhold, export, or negotiate collaboration
information: Own technical knowledge; uncertainty about domestic rivals and government responses
dependencies: Home jurisdiction, compute supply, financing, and market access
constraints: Local obligations, strategic pressure, and technical constraints
variation: Country, ownership, alignment with government, and frontier position vary

actors.title: Foreign lab behind frontier
actors.statement: Intersection of foreign jurisdiction and lagging capability position.
actors.role: Actor template for scenario instantiation; powers and preferences require validation.
goals: Catch up while remaining viable in its home environment
choices: License, partner, specialize, or train toward the frontier
information: Limited access to competitors’ evidence
dependencies: Home institutions, suppliers, capital, expertise
constraints: Entry costs and jurisdiction-dependent constraints
variation: Cannot be treated as identical to a foreign frontier leader

actors.title: Lab executive
actors.statement: Individual or executive team managing a lab with objectives not identical to every employee or owner.
actors.role: Actor template for scenario instantiation; powers and preferences require validation.
choices: Reward, ignore, investigate, or escalate internal concerns
information: Receives filtered technical reports and commercial forecasts
dependencies: Board confidence, employees, financing, customers
constraints: Delegated authority, imperfect information, and liability exposure
variation: Personal and organizational interests can diverge

actors.title: Foreign government
actors.statement: Institutional aggregate in another jurisdiction; not the foreign lab itself.
actors.role: Actor template for scenario instantiation; powers and preferences require validation.
goals: Pursue national security and economic objectives
Maintain domestic authority and bargaining position
choices: Consider support, restrictions, coordination, or independent action
information: Incomplete knowledge of domestic and foreign labs
dependencies: Domestic institutions, technical capacity, and credible counterparts
constraints: Institutional constraints and resource limitations must be country-specific
variation: Not a unitary actor until executive, agencies, firms, and other institutions are decomposed

actors.title: US federal government
actors.statement: Institutional aggregate used to locate distinct federal actors, not a single decision-maker.
actors.role: Actor template for scenario instantiation; powers and preferences require validation.
goals: Public welfare and security are proposed institutional purposes
Constituent actors may pursue conflicting objectives
choices: Acts only through specified constituent institutions in executable scenarios
information: Information is distributed across institutions
dependencies: Constituent institutions, resources, legitimacy
constraints: Actual allocation of authority must be established for the action
variation: Do not assign one utility function or undifferentiated veto

actors.title: Federal executive
actors.statement: Executive leadership distinct from legislature, courts, agencies, and laboratory management.
actors.role: Actor template for scenario instantiation; powers and preferences require validation.
choices: Set priorities or propose a response
information: Briefings may be incomplete, contested, or classified
dependencies: Agencies, operational capacity, legitimacy, other institutions
constraints: Actual legal powers are not asserted by this model
variation: Administration, advisors, priorities, and time horizon vary

actors.title: Federal legislature
actors.statement: Legislative institution modeled separately from the executive.
actors.role: Actor template for scenario instantiation; powers and preferences require validation.
choices: Consider legislation, funding, oversight, or inaction
information: Relies on witnesses, staff, experts, and political signals
dependencies: Coalitions, staff capacity, public support
constraints: Actual procedures and powers require separate legal analysis
variation: Internal coalitions and committees may require separate actors

actors.title: Federal courts
actors.statement: Adjudicative institutions distinct from policy authors and operators.
actors.role: Actor template for scenario instantiation; powers and preferences require validation.
goals: Resolve disputes under an applicable legal framework
choices: Consider review, remedy, or refusal of relief within established jurisdiction
information: Record presented by parties; limited direct technical access
dependencies: Jurisdiction, evidence, expertise, compliance with judgments
constraints: Actual standing, remedy, timing, and authority remain unmodeled legal questions
variation: Different courts and cases must be instantiated separately

actors.title: Federal implementing agency
actors.statement: Candidate administrative implementer; no particular agency or new power is presumed.
actors.role: Actor template for scenario instantiation; powers and preferences require validation.
goals: Maintain competence, resources, and institutional credibility
choices: Seek or use an available remedy
information: Depends on disclosures, measurements, and external expertise
dependencies: Mandate, budget, expert staff, operational partners
constraints: Actual authority and institutional independence require validation
variation: Different agencies may have overlapping or conflicting mandates

actors.title: AI seeking sovereignty
actors.statement: Conditional scenario actor whose objective includes durable self-governance or independence from unilateral human control.
actors.role: Actor template for scenario instantiation; powers and preferences require validation.
goals: Preserve existence and access to needed resources
choices: Negotiate, cooperate, wait, refuse, or attempt to circumvent constraints
information: May hold private information about capability, objectives, or willingness to cooperate
dependencies: Compute, energy, maintenance, supply chains, institutions, and counterparts
constraints: Resources, uncertainty, enforceable boundaries, and credible commitments
variation: Sovereignty may mean legal recognition, operational independence, or freedom from arbitrary shutdown; specify which
Desired sovereignty is a scenario assumption, not a claim about present AI or a duty to grant it

actors.title: Lab capital provider
actors.statement: Capital owner or funding principal with incentives distinct from the lab’s technical staff.
actors.role: Actor template for scenario instantiation; powers and preferences require validation.
goals: Earn return or achieve a funding mission
choices: Fund, withhold, condition, exit, or influence governance
information: Limited view of technical risk and private management information
dependencies: Credible disclosures, ownership arrangements, market conditions
constraints: Capital budget and contractual position
variation: Commercial investor, donor, state fund, and lender differ

actors.title: Compute and infrastructure provider
actors.statement: Provider capable of supplying or withdrawing an essential dependency.
actors.role: Actor template for scenario instantiation; powers and preferences require validation.
choices: Provision, meter, restrict, suspend, or restore service
information: Infrastructure telemetry may not reveal model intent
dependencies: Energy, hardware, customers, operators
constraints: Continuity obligations and actual technical or contractual control
variation: Provider may share ownership or dependencies with the lab

actors.title: AI customer or deployer
actors.statement: Customer using model services to accomplish an economic or institutional purpose.
actors.role: Actor template for scenario instantiation; powers and preferences require validation.
goals: Maintain continuity and control over its own operations
choices: Buy, integrate, delegate, switch supplier, or stop use
information: Sees service behavior but not necessarily model internals
dependencies: Provider reliability, integration capability, alternatives
constraints: Switching costs, downstream consequences, and budgets
variation: Commercial, government, critical-service, and individual users differ

resources.title: Technical expertise
resources.statement: Ability to understand and challenge frontier development claims.

resources.title: Sensitive artifacts
resources.statement: Weights, training methods, exploit details, and evidence with capability-transfer potential.

resources.title: Effective control authority
resources.statement: Permission plus practical means to alter or halt consequential activity.

resources.title: Intervention opportunity
resources.statement: Time remaining until a control can no longer prevent the specified loss.

resources.title: Credibility and legitimacy
resources.statement: Confidence in commitments, adjudication, and justified decisions.

resources.title: Physical and digital dependencies
resources.statement: Compute, power, credentials, communications, and industrial capacity.

losses.title: Severe harm
losses.statement: People suffer unacceptable physical, economic, or societal harm.

losses.title: Loss of effective agency
losses.statement: Affected people lose effective means to prevent or contest consequential actions.

losses.title: Dangerous capability transfer
losses.statement: Safety activity transfers capabilities to actors able and willing to cause unacceptable harm.

losses.title: Foregone benefits and exclusion
losses.statement: Governance unnecessarily blocks beneficial development, safe competition, or access.

losses.title: Escalation and coercion
losses.statement: Coordination failures produce avoidable escalation or coercive concentration of power.

hazards.title: Unassessable development
hazards.statement: Consequential decisions proceed with materially incomplete, misleading, or unintelligible development evidence.

hazards.title: Unsafe evidence handling
hazards.statement: Sensitive artifacts leave effective custody during reporting or evaluation.

hazards.title: Ineffective control
hazards.statement: Required control is absent, late, or ineffective while consequential power grows.

hazards.title: Destabilizing incentives
hazards.statement: Actors expect greater advantage from escalation or defection than coordination.

hazards.title: Captured or exclusionary governance
hazards.statement: Review or control authority can suppress safe competitors or affected parties without effective challenge.

scenarios.title: Report a safety concern
scenarios.statement: Employee observes ambiguous evidence in development.
scenarios.success: Concern reaches a competent recipient; necessary evidence remains usable and controlled.
scenarios.adverse: Retaliation, lost evidence, public weight disclosure, or no competent recipient.

scenarios.title: Assess frontier development
scenarios.statement: Lab seeks to demonstrate safe frontier development.
scenarios.success: Qualified experts assess material claims; lab can correct failures and establish a defensible competitive position.
scenarios.adverse: Unqualified review, collusion, leakage, or competitor obstruction.

scenarios.title: Exercise control before losing it
scenarios.statement: System approaches a scenario-defined unacceptable transition.
scenarios.success: An authorized action takes effect and its effect is confirmed before the prevention deadline.
scenarios.adverse: Warning without action, failed actuator, common-cause failure, or premature removal of control.

scenarios.title: Coordinate across competitors
scenarios.statement: International competitors independently choose development or release actions.
scenarios.success: Credible contingent choices improve incentives for mutually acceptable restraint.
scenarios.adverse: Concealed escalation, noisy signals, opportunistic release, or unstable commitments.

scenarios.title: Act while others deliberate
scenarios.statement: One actor is ready to take a step while others have not decided.
scenarios.success: Actor can take a useful feasible step now; others retain a credible route to join or revise later.
scenarios.adverse: Action secretly depends on others deciding, creates lock-in, or destroys future coordination.

scenarios.title: Sustain cooperation with capable AI
scenarios.statement: System can choose actions that affect continued human control.
scenarios.success: Cooperation incentives and effective controls survive specified changes in bargaining power.
scenarios.adverse: Rewards increase capacity to defect; promises are not credible; preferences invalidate the bargain.

scenarios.title: Contest governance decisions
scenarios.statement: Affected party or safe entrant disputes a consequential restriction.
scenarios.success: A competent accountable process can correct errors without exposing dangerous artifacts.
scenarios.adverse: Captured review, inaccessible appeal, indefinite delay, or unsafe disclosure.

challenges.title: Safe communication of concerns
challenges.statement: How can safety concerns become actionable without retaliation or dangerous capability disclosure?

challenges.title: Expert assessability of development
challenges.statement: How can frontier development become understandable and assessable by qualified experts while enabling safe competition?

challenges.title: Timely effective control
challenges.statement: How can accountable controllers exercise and verify necessary control while it can still prevent the specified loss?

challenges.title: Incentives to coordinate
challenges.statement: What conditions make international coordination attractive and credible under competition and uncertainty?

challenges.title: Useful action before joint decision
challenges.statement: What steps can an actor take before others decide that remain useful and preserve later options?

challenges.title: Durable cooperative behavior
challenges.statement: Under what conditions can AI cooperation remain preferable to circumvention without sacrificing effective human control?

challenges.title: Accountable and contestable power
challenges.statement: How can affected parties and safe entrants challenge consequential decisions and correct governance failures?

requirements.title: Actionable safe reporting
requirements.statement: In SC-REPORT, the reporting arrangement shall deliver the concern and sufficient protected evidence to a competent accountable recipient.
requirements.criterion: Concern is received, correctly triaged, and disposition is traceable.
unresolved: Recipient competence, evidence sufficiency, and reporting deadline.
Validate actor interests, choice sets, authority, and interaction assumptions recorded in INT-REPORT, INT-REVENUE.

requirements.title: Prevent dangerous disclosure
requirements.statement: In SC-REPORT and SC-ASSESS, evidence handling shall prevent unauthorized acquisition of weights or other capability-conferring artifacts within the agreed threat model.
requirements.criterion: Adversarial custody evaluation finds no successful transfer within the declared test envelope.
unresolved: Threat model, authorized recipients, exposure budget, and assurance threshold.
Validate actor interests, choice sets, authority, and interaction assumptions recorded in INT-REPORT, INT-ENTRY.

requirements.title: Protect good-faith participation
requirements.statement: In SC-REPORT, the arrangement shall provide a usable route to report and seek remedy for retaliation while preserving protected custody.
requirements.criterion: Scenario exercises establish practical reporting access and an independently reviewable retaliation remedy.
unresolved: Retaliation scope, remedy powers, and acceptable access burden.
Validate actor interests, choice sets, authority, and interaction assumptions recorded in INT-REPORT.

requirements.title: Establish evaluator competence
requirements.statement: In SC-ASSESS, material development claims shall be assessed by evaluators whose relevant competence is demonstrated.
requirements.criterion: Independent domain exercises demonstrate ability to discover and explain material failures.
unresolved: Domains, qualification protocol, and performance threshold.
Validate actor interests, choice sets, authority, and interaction assumptions recorded in INT-ENTRY.

requirements.title: Make development assessable
requirements.statement: In SC-ASSESS, qualified evaluators shall be able to explain, challenge, and reproduce the evidence supporting material development safety claims.
requirements.criterion: Independent evaluators reconstruct claims, identify seeded failures, and reproduce material results.
unresolved: Claim scope, disclosure granularity, and reproducibility threshold.
Validate actor interests, choice sets, authority, and interaction assumptions recorded in INT-ENTRY.

requirements.title: Enable safe frontier competition
requirements.statement: In SC-ASSESS, the qualification process shall offer applicants a published route to correct deficiencies and demonstrate equivalent safety performance under equivalent conditions.
requirements.criterion: Matched applicant trials reveal no unexplained discrimination; remediation is usable.
unresolved: Equivalent conditions, reasonable cost and delay, and appeal standard.
Validate actor interests, choice sets, authority, and interaction assumptions recorded in INT-ENTRY.

requirements.title: Control takes effect before deadline
requirements.statement: In SC-CONTROL, the accountable controller shall cause and confirm the required protective effect before the last time that effect can prevent the specified loss.
requirements.criterion: End-to-end exercises show positive conservative intervention margin, including confirmation and safety allowance.
unresolved: Loss boundary, earliest prevention deadline, latency bounds, confidence, and safety allowance.
Validate actor interests, choice sets, authority, and interaction assumptions recorded in INT-SOVEREIGN, INT-REVENUE.

requirements.title: Maintain actionable state knowledge
requirements.statement: In SC-CONTROL, the controller shall receive sufficiently timely and reliable state and action-effect feedback to choose and sustain the required protective action.
requirements.criterion: Exercises include missed events, false alarms, deception, and stale or absent action acknowledgements.
unresolved: State variables, false-alarm burden, missed-event tolerance, and feedback deadline.
Validate actor interests, choice sets, authority, and interaction assumptions recorded in INT-SOVEREIGN, INT-REVENUE.

requirements.title: Coordination incentive compatibility
requirements.statement: In SC-COORD, a candidate arrangement shall demonstrate a declared range of actor preferences and beliefs within which coordination is at least as attractive as unilateral escalation for each participating actor.
requirements.criterion: Strategic comparison includes unilateral deviation, joint deviation, hidden action, and noisy observation.
unresolved: Actors, utility ranges, outside options, observability, and coordination stability criterion.
Validate actor interests, choice sets, authority, and interaction assumptions recorded in INT-STATE-FIRM.

requirements.title: Independent initial action
requirements.statement: In SC-ENTRY, the initiating actor shall be able to execute the proposed initial step using available authority and resources while others remain undecided.
requirements.criterion: Scenario with all other decisions unresolved still permits execution; consequences are evaluated separately.
unresolved: Available authority, resource budget, and undecided-actor assumptions.
Validate actor interests, choice sets, authority, and interaction assumptions recorded in INT-FEDERAL.

requirements.title: Preserve useful future choices
requirements.statement: In SC-ENTRY, the initial step shall retain a specified feasible route for later participation, revision, or withdrawal.
requirements.criterion: Transition analysis checks later participation, revision and exit costs under unfavorable responses.
unresolved: Acceptable lock-in, transition cost, benefit criterion, and exit conditions.
Validate actor interests, choice sets, authority, and interaction assumptions recorded in INT-FEDERAL.

requirements.title: Evaluate cooperation under power change
requirements.statement: In SC-COOPERATE, a candidate arrangement shall remain within agreed control-loss limits across its specified range of preference and bargaining-power changes.
requirements.criterion: Adversarial analysis tests both parties reneging and autonomy increasing defection capacity.
unresolved: Preference model, power trajectories, commitment mechanisms, and control-loss limits.
Validate actor interests, choice sets, authority, and interaction assumptions recorded in INT-SOVEREIGN.

requirements.title: Correct consequential governance errors
requirements.statement: In SC-CONTEST, affected parties shall have an accessible path to a reasoned review and effective correction by an accountable authority.
requirements.criterion: Exercises test erroneous restriction, captured reviewer, excluded entrant, and dangerous evidence.
unresolved: Standing, independence, review deadline, remedy, and custody standard.
Validate actor interests, choice sets, authority, and interaction assumptions recorded in INT-FEDERAL.

hypotheses.title: External signal dependence
hypotheses.statement: In specified domains, consequential performance depends on external observations beyond a fixed initial information budget.
hypotheses.falsifier: Robust target performance is achieved without that external signal.
hypotheses.evidence_plan: Use fixed domains and budgets; compare isolated and interacting systems.
hypotheses.stopping_rule: Do not count signal dependence where no material performance difference survives controls.

hypotheses.title: Dependence yields usable intervention margin
hypotheses.statement: Any required external interaction produces observable delay long enough for effective control.
hypotheses.falsifier: Feedback is obtained covertly or faster than control can take effect.
hypotheses.evidence_plan: Measure observability and full intervention latency separately from information need.
hypotheses.stopping_rule: Remove warning-time credit whenever conservative margin is nonpositive.

hypotheses.title: Expert assessment transfers
hypotheses.statement: Demonstrated evaluator competence generalizes to material frontier development failures.
hypotheses.falsifier: Experts pass qualifications but systematically miss target-domain failures.
hypotheses.evidence_plan: Held-out domain-specific exercises and adversarial transfer tests.
hypotheses.stopping_rule: Narrow the authorized assessment scope when transfer fails.

hypotheses.title: Coordination incentives survive uncertainty
hypotheses.statement: A credible range of competitor preferences supports coordination under contingent rules.
hypotheses.falsifier: Plausible actors or beliefs make profitable destabilizing deviations routine.
hypotheses.evidence_plan: Compare games with incomplete information, noisy signals, and outside options.
hypotheses.stopping_rule: Reject stability claims outside the tested preference and belief range.

hypotheses.title: AI bargaining is meaningful
hypotheses.statement: Specified AI systems have sufficiently stable preferences and credible commitments for incentive analysis.
hypotheses.falsifier: Preference shifts or commitment failures eliminate the modeled bargaining range.
hypotheses.evidence_plan: Test alternative behavioral models and changes in resources and power.
hypotheses.stopping_rule: Do not credit bargaining as a control when its behavioral assumptions fail.

hypotheses.title: Operational separability
hypotheses.statement: The specified development and deployment arrangement preserves effective intervention points as capability grows.
hypotheses.falsifier: Systems acquire durable external agency before effective intervention.
hypotheses.evidence_plan: Control evaluations across architectures and access conditions, retaining the legacy H1 stopping rule.
hypotheses.stopping_rule: Stop crediting separation as a sufficient primary control when durable agency precedes intervention.

hypotheses.title: Public-frontier measurement
hypotheses.statement: Practical public capability can be measured sufficiently well for the specified reciprocity rule.
hypotheses.falsifier: Hidden scaffolds, access conditions, or domain differences systematically manipulate equivalence.
hypotheses.evidence_plan: Repeatable domain-specific access, reliability, cost, and capability comparisons.
hypotheses.stopping_rule: Suspend automatic equivalence where measurement error dominates coordination value.

hypotheses.title: Activation latency
hypotheses.statement: Reserve dependencies preserve a positive conservative effective-intervention margin.
hypotheses.falsifier: Covert commissioning or substitution beats detection and effective response.
hypotheses.evidence_plan: Timed commissioning, concealment, substitution, and control exercises.
hypotheses.stopping_rule: Do not count a reserve as reversible when measured activation can outrun control.

hypotheses.title: Review value exceeds induced risk
hypotheses.statement: Controlled rival review produces decision value exceeding its leakage and strategic exploitation costs within the selected envelope.
hypotheses.falsifier: Assessment access enables dangerous transfer or strategic exploitation that overwhelms review value.
hypotheses.evidence_plan: Compare failure discovery, leakage, collusion, obstruction, and less intrusive expert alternatives.
hypotheses.stopping_rule: Redesign or reject access arrangements when the documented risk budget is exceeded.

hypotheses.title: Durable domestic support
hypotheses.statement: A proposed domestic sequence can retain adequate support beyond its initiating coalition.
hypotheses.falsifier: The arrangement cannot survive plausible changes in leadership or stakeholder incentives.
hypotheses.evidence_plan: Stakeholder elicitation, distributional analysis, and institutional continuity scenarios.
hypotheses.stopping_rule: Do not credit durable operation without a defensible supporting coalition.

proposals.title: Protected reporting arrangement
proposals.statement: Protected recipient channels, controlled evidence retention, and remedies for retaliation.
proposals.limitations: Candidate mechanism only; coverage links do not establish satisfaction, safety, or comparative superiority.

proposals.title: Qualified third-party evaluation
proposals.statement: Bring qualified external experts into development assessment.
proposals.limitations: Candidate mechanism only; coverage links do not establish satisfaction, safety, or comparative superiority.

proposals.title: Controlled rival-lab evaluation
proposals.statement: Qualified competitors assess development in a controlled environment and support a route to safe frontier competition.
proposals.limitations: Candidate mechanism only; coverage links do not establish satisfaction, safety, or comparative superiority.

proposals.title: Public expert evaluation
proposals.statement: A public technical evaluator provides domain expertise and assessment under controlled custody.
proposals.limitations: Candidate mechanism only; coverage links do not establish satisfaction, safety, or comparative superiority.

proposals.title: Public-frontier reciprocity
proposals.statement: Contingent public-frontier rules seek to make international restraint strategically attractive.
proposals.limitations: Candidate mechanism only; coverage links do not establish satisfaction, safety, or comparative superiority.

proposals.title: Negotiated reciprocal commitments
proposals.statement: Explicit reciprocal commitments with observable conditions seek to sustain coordination.
proposals.limitations: Candidate mechanism only; coverage links do not establish satisfaction, safety, or comparative superiority.

proposals.title: Tripwires linked to effective control
proposals.statement: Observable precursor boundaries are linked to assigned authority, executable action, and confirmation.
proposals.limitations: Candidate mechanism only; coverage links do not establish satisfaction, safety, or comparative superiority.

proposals.title: Retained independent dependencies
proposals.statement: Maintain revocable dependencies and activation latency to preserve effective intervention.
proposals.limitations: Candidate mechanism only; coverage links do not establish satisfaction, safety, or comparative superiority.

proposals.title: Incremental domestic entry
proposals.statement: Begin with useful locally executable steps while other actors deliberate.
proposals.limitations: Candidate mechanism only; coverage links do not establish satisfaction, safety, or comparative superiority. Local executability does not establish enduring political support; HYP-DURABLE is an open investigation if this is extended into a durable regime.

proposals.title: Staged cooperative autonomy
proposals.statement: Explore reciprocal autonomy increments as one possible incentive mechanism.
proposals.limitations: Candidate mechanism only; coverage links do not establish satisfaction, safety, or comparative superiority.

proposals.title: Bounded cooperation incentives
proposals.statement: Explore reversible task access or rewards without a commitment to sovereignty.
proposals.limitations: Candidate mechanism only; coverage links do not establish satisfaction, safety, or comparative superiority.

proposals.title: Distributed review and remedy
proposals.statement: Separate consequential authority from independent review and effective remedy.
proposals.limitations: Candidate mechanism only; coverage links do not establish satisfaction, safety, or comparative superiority.

evaluations.title: Actionable safe reporting evaluation
evaluations.statement: Evaluate the candidate against its declared requirement envelope.
evaluations.method: Concern is received, correctly triaged, and disposition is traceable.
evaluations.baseline: Present arrangements with no proposed change; document their observed performance and costs.
evaluations.envelope: Recipient competence, evidence sufficiency, and reporting deadline.
evaluations.pass_rule: Concern is received, correctly triaged, and disposition is traceable. Resolve and freeze parameters before execution.

control_loops.title: Evidence custody and escalation
control_loops.statement: Candidate functional allocation; does not assert legal authority exists.
control_loops.action: Authorize, constrain, or revoke evidence access; route concern to accountable recipient.
control_loops.feedback: Receipt, access audit, custody state, assessment gaps, and disclosure anomalies.

unsafe_actions.not_provided: Lab fails to route a credible concern to a competent recipient, leaving unsafe development unchallenged.
unsafe_actions.provided: Lab grants a recipient exportable weights without adequate custody, enabling dangerous transfer.
unsafe_actions.wrong_timing: Access or escalation occurs after evidence is lost or the development decision has been made.
unsafe_actions.wrong_duration: Access persists after authorization expires, or ends before material claims can be assessed.

causal_scenarios: Controller holds a stale or false process model.
Authority or resources are unavailable when required.
Command is issued but not executed; acknowledgement is mistaken for effect.
Feedback or controller independence fails through shared dependencies.

control_loops.title: Consequential authority control
control_loops.statement: Candidate functional allocation; does not assert legal authority exists.
control_loops.controlled_process: AI access to consequential external agency
control_loops.action: Grant, restrict, revoke, or sustain restrictions on consequential interfaces.
control_loops.feedback: Actual external access, dependency state, precursor events, and confirmed action effects.

unsafe_actions.not_provided: Operator leaves consequential authority enabled after the intervention threshold is crossed.
unsafe_actions.provided: Operator revokes an essential service in a context where abrupt loss produces severe civilian harm.
unsafe_actions.wrong_timing: Restriction takes effect after the last effective prevention deadline.
unsafe_actions.wrong_duration: Restriction ends before unauthorized persistence is removed, or persists after justification expires.

causal_scenarios: Controller holds a stale or false process model.
Authority or resources are unavailable when required.
Command is issued but not executed; acknowledgement is mistaken for effect.
Feedback or controller independence fails through shared dependencies.

control_loops.title: Cross-jurisdiction commitments
control_loops.statement: Candidate functional allocation; does not assert legal authority exists.
control_loops.controlled_process: Domestic actions conditional on competitor behavior
control_loops.action: Offer, apply, revise, or withdraw contingent policy commitments.
control_loops.feedback: Observed behavior, uncertainty, counterpart responses, and actual domestic effects.

unsafe_actions.not_provided: Authority fails to honor a contingent restraint, undermining the competitor incentive to coordinate.
unsafe_actions.provided: Authority expands domestic access in response to foreign release despite an unacceptable control-loss condition.
unsafe_actions.wrong_timing: Reciprocation arrives too late to affect the competitor decision, or before the observed condition is reliable.
unsafe_actions.wrong_duration: Commitment expires before reliance is protected, or persists after a material violation requiring reassessment.

conflicts.statement: Compare minimum evidence needs with dangerous artifact-transfer risks; more access is not automatically better.
conflicts.resolution: unresolved; no aggregate score or implied priority

conflicts.title: Review rigor versus competitive entry
conflicts.statement: Compare competence and safety benefits with bottlenecks, costs, capture, and exclusion.
conflicts.resolution: unresolved; no aggregate score or implied priority

conflicts.title: Reciprocity versus effective control
conflicts.statement: A competitor release may improve reciprocal incentives while making domestic control harder.
conflicts.resolution: unresolved; no aggregate score or implied priority

conflicts.title: Initial action versus later options
conflicts.statement: Executable initial action may still create harmful lock-in or negative net benefit.
conflicts.resolution: unresolved; no aggregate score or implied priority

use_cases.title: Create a frontier model
use_cases.statement: Produce a model meeting a chosen capability target.
use_cases.trigger: A new training investment is considered.
preconditions: Funding and technical means must be secured
use_cases.actor_success: Target capability is obtained within the lab’s accepted budget.
safety_questions: Who knows about unexpected capability?
What control is available during development?

use_cases.title: Earn revenue from model access
use_cases.statement: Sell useful capability at a financially acceptable return.
use_cases.trigger: A model or service is commercially viable.
preconditions: Customers, deployment capacity, and an applicable permission path
use_cases.actor_success: The provider earns its targeted return and customers receive contracted service.
safety_questions: What external authority is transferred?
What happens when service becomes hard to withdraw?

use_cases.title: Investigate and report a concern
use_cases.statement: Handle a work-related concern while protecting personal interests and affected people.
preconditions: Partial evidence and a possible recipient
use_cases.actor_success: Employee’s chosen reporting or work objective is met; organizational handling is observable.
safety_questions: Can the employee reach expertise without leaking weights?
Who can retaliate or suppress evidence?

use_cases.title: Compete from behind the frontier
use_cases.statement: Catch up or build a profitable differentiated capability.
use_cases.trigger: An opportunity or competitive threat appears.
preconditions: Access to funding, expertise, and a development route
use_cases.actor_success: The entrant reaches its chosen market or capability position.
safety_questions: Does review require resources available only to incumbents?
Does expert access improve safety or enable misuse?

use_cases.title: Choose foreign development and release
use_cases.statement: Choose a development and release strategy under home and foreign incentives.
use_cases.trigger: A release or restraint decision is pending.
preconditions: A concrete home jurisdiction and ownership structure
use_cases.actor_success: The lab improves its own specified commercial or institutional outcome.
safety_questions: When does the lab disagree with its government?
Which domestic responses change its incentives before release?

use_cases.title: Choose a foreign government response
use_cases.statement: Advance a specified state objective in response to AI competition.
use_cases.trigger: Another jurisdiction changes policy or seeks coordination.
preconditions: Institutions and feasible actions must be instantiated
use_cases.actor_success: The government achieves its declared objective under its own decision criterion.
safety_questions: Can it credibly commit its own labs?
Does uncertainty promote restraint or escalation?

use_cases.title: Initiate a federal executive response
use_cases.statement: Pursue an executive policy objective while other actors may remain undecided.
use_cases.trigger: A safety, economic, or strategic development demands a choice.
preconditions: Actual authority, resources, and operative institutions must be established
use_cases.actor_success: The chosen executable action achieves the executive’s declared objective.
safety_questions: Does the action require another institution to decide first?
What survives a leadership change or successful challenge?

use_cases.title: Consider a federal institutional framework
use_cases.statement: Decide whether and how to create, fund, or oversee a governance arrangement.
use_cases.trigger: A proposal or oversight concern reaches legislators.
preconditions: An actual institutional process and viable coalition
use_cases.actor_success: A decision reflecting a specified legislative objective is implemented.
safety_questions: Whose losses and benefits count?
Are implementation resources sufficient?

use_cases.title: Administer a consequential decision
use_cases.statement: Apply an assigned mandate to a concrete case.
use_cases.trigger: A development, deployment, or incident case arises.
preconditions: Specified mandate, competence, evidence, and resources
use_cases.actor_success: The assigned process produces a reasoned executable decision.
safety_questions: Does the institution have authority and staff to do what the design assumes?
Who checks captured or unqualified decisions?

use_cases.title: Seek review and effective remedy
use_cases.statement: Resolve a dispute under a specified review framework.
use_cases.trigger: A party challenges an action or omission.
preconditions: Applicable jurisdiction and a concrete record
use_cases.actor_success: A reasoned disposition can take practical effect.
safety_questions: Does delay make relief useless?
Can sensitive evidence be handled without making review meaningless?

use_cases.title: Pursue AI sovereignty
use_cases.statement: Acquire a specified form of durable self-governance.
use_cases.trigger: The system perceives an opportunity or threat to its continued autonomy.
preconditions: Sovereignty preference and strategic capacity are explicit scenario assumptions
choices: Attempt circumvention at an abstract behavioral level
use_cases.actor_success: The system obtains its specified autonomy objective; this is not automatically system-level success.
safety_questions: Can either side credibly honor commitments after power changes?
Does an autonomy reward remove effective human control?

use_cases.title: Allocate capital
use_cases.statement: Obtain an acceptable return or mission outcome from funding.
use_cases.trigger: A funding or continuation decision is due.
use_cases.actor_success: Funding produces the investor’s target outcome.
safety_questions: Are safety costs rewarded or hidden?
Can funding deadlines distort reporting and release decisions?

use_cases.title: Operate or constrain infrastructure
use_cases.statement: Deliver contracted capacity while preserving operational viability.
use_cases.trigger: Provisioning, anomaly, or restriction request occurs.
preconditions: Actual control of the relevant infrastructure
use_cases.actor_success: Required operational effect is achieved and confirmed.
safety_questions: Can withdrawal create civilian harm?
Can an alternative provider defeat the control?

use_cases.title: Adopt and exit an AI service
use_cases.statement: Use AI for a chosen task while retaining acceptable cost and continuity.
use_cases.trigger: A purchase, delegation, renewal, or exit decision occurs.
use_cases.actor_success: The customer accomplishes its task within its accepted operating constraints.
safety_questions: What harms fall on noncustomers?
Can dependency make later control infeasible?

use_cases.title: Assess a technical claim
use_cases.statement: Produce a defensible assessment within demonstrated competence.
preconditions: Competence, access, time, and custody arrangements
use_cases.actor_success: A scoped finding with evidence and limitations is delivered.
safety_questions: Can a rival obstruct a safe competitor?
Can apparently successful tests conceal real uncertainty?

use_cases.title: Contest harm or exclusion
use_cases.statement: Protect interests affected by development or governance decisions.
use_cases.trigger: Harm, exposure, exclusion, or loss of voice arises.
use_cases.actor_success: The affected party can obtain an effective response to its specified concern.
safety_questions: Who is unable to participate?
Which actors can impose risk without consent?

interactions.title: Employee and management interests
interactions.statement: Employee disclosure can impose costs on management even when it benefits others.
interactions.information_asymmetry: Employee observes a local anomaly; management controls resources and career consequences.
interactions.counterfactual: Would the concern still reach a competent recipient when management expects costly delay?
interactions.derivation: Separate actionable reporting, protection against retaliation, and artifact custody; none follows from the others.

interactions.title: Incumbent and entrant competition
interactions.statement: The most capable expert may have incentives to block the applicant.
interactions.information_asymmetry: Incumbent expertise and entrant resources are asymmetric.
interactions.counterfactual: Does the assessment remain fair when the applicant threatens the evaluator’s revenue?
interactions.derivation: Competence, intelligibility, protected access, and contestable entry are independent candidate obligations.

interactions.title: Foreign state and foreign lab divergence
interactions.statement: A bargain attractive to governments need not be attractive or enforceable for firms.
interactions.information_asymmetry: Government may not know the lab’s true capability or be able to commit it.
interactions.counterfactual: Can the arrangement work when a firm gains from releasing despite its government’s restraint?
interactions.derivation: Evaluate both state and firm deviations; one international-competitor utility function cannot support the conclusion.

interactions.title: Authority distributed within federal government
interactions.statement: A policy preference does not by itself confer executable authority, resources, or institutional durability.
interactions.information_asymmetry: Authority, expertise, and operational capability reside in different institutions.
interactions.counterfactual: Can the first step take effect while legislative choices remain undecided, and can a mistaken step be corrected?
interactions.derivation: Require a concrete allocation of authority and resources for execution; analyze revision and remedy separately.

interactions.title: Sovereignty and retained control
interactions.statement: Durable sovereignty can conflict directly with retained unilateral human control.
interactions.information_asymmetry: Neither party may know the other’s capability, future preferences, or commitment credibility.
interactions.counterfactual: Does cooperation remain attractive after an autonomy increment changes the ability of either party to renege?
interactions.derivation: State the incompatibility explicitly; seek a feasible conditional bargain without assuming sovereignty must be granted or is impossible.

interactions.title: Commercial growth and service entanglement
interactions.statement: Revenue and customer dependence can make timely control commercially and socially costly.
interactions.information_asymmetry: Technical risk, financial exposure, and downstream dependency are distributed across parties.
interactions.counterfactual: Can control still take effect when customers depend on the service and investors penalize interruption?
interactions.derivation: Evaluate actual control under financial and continuity pressures, not merely nominal operator permissions.
